claims.finding: A new SCHEDULE 13D — control or activist intent, not a passive 13G — was accepted 2026-07-09T21:02:45 by self-filer CIK 0001734341, sixteen minutes before a Form 4, two days after an item 5.02 8-K (2026-07-07T20:16), and four days before director Daniel Englander bought $398k of stock in a single open-market purchase that raised his holding 117%; after those Form 4s on 2026-07-13/14 the company then filed nothing at all for seven weeks until the print itself.
claims.why_not_priced: The capture contains zero news items for YEXT across five sweeps — the only external link in the entire corpus is a marketwirenews page announcing the earnings date — so no wire story, preview or sell-side note exists here to have carried it, and 13D bodies are not stored, meaning the holder, the size and the stated intent were never summarised anywhere a price could react to. Context that makes it matter: the CEO withdrew a $9-per-share take-private proposal on 2026-02-02 citing financing, the company simultaneously authorised a $150m buyback, and per the retail thread it borrowed $50m at 10.25% to fund repurchases that at the prevailing price would retire roughly a quarter of the shares. If a control-intent stake at a company 25% below a recently withdrawn bid were priced, the stock would not still be 26.1% below its 52-week high.
claims.independence: Corroborated from a different source in the corpus: the Stocktwits thread at docs/601a3e5ab27afe4e9bca5545757b06c38a19f530.txt (no URL; kind: social) independently flags the same purchase in an insider-buy roundup on 2026-07-14 ('$YEXT — $398K single buy by insider Daniel Englander, +117% stake increase (Jul 13)') with a link to https://filingtracker.ai/filing/1289438/0001628280-26-048066 , and separately describes the $50m 10.25% borrowing behind the buyback. That is retail paraphrase, so the independent leg is weaker than the filing metadata it confirms.
